clue.text: Illness comes around holiday time

parts.note: C, short for circa, means around or approximately
HOL is a common short form of holiday
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone falls sick just as the holidays arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is a serious infectious disease, so it is an example of an illness.

clue.text: Short coffee-colour garment

indicators.note: short means the coffee word loses its last letter

parts.note: cafe is French for coffee
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A brief coffee-brown item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A caftan is a long loose robe, a type of garment.

clue.text: Wild ass threw stones

definitions.meaning: a Roman siege catapult that hurled rocks bore the same name

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an Asian wild ass and an ancient stone-throwing catapult.

clue.text: Curtains available rather in Europe than further east

parts.note: EU is the European Union
taken as written
Asia lies further east than Europe

explanation.surface: Something is more easily obtained in Europe than in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtains' is slang for death, here an assisted one; 'available rather in' simply joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Euthanasia means a deliberately ended life, and curtains is slang for the end or death.

clue.text: Late Arab leader when downhearted

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
sad means downhearted

explanation.surface: A dead Arab ruler is remembered as gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hafez al-Assad was the late president of Syria, an Arab leader.

clue.text: A short drink and journalist is marked for life

indicators.note: short tells us to cut the final letter off the drink word

parts.note: brandy is a drink
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A tot of spirits with a newspaperman leaves someone scarred for good.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' belongs to the surface reading 'A short drink'; it adds no letter, since the brand trimmed from the spirit already supplies the word's start.
explanation.definitionFit: To be branded is to be burnt with a permanent mark, hence marked for life.

clue.text: Reporter once said to be drunk

indicators.note: said to be signals that the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a beverage is something drunk

explanation.surface: A one-time journalist was rumoured to be intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: William Beveridge wrote the 1942 Beveridge Report that founded Britain's welfare state, so he was a reporter in the sense of a report's author.
explanation.definitionFit: Beveridge authored a famous government report, so he was a reporter in a historical sense.

clue.text: Current cold wind direction spoils the complexion

parts.note: AC is alternating current
NE, north-east, is the direction the cold wind blows from

explanation.surface: A biting wind from the north-east roughens the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition of spots that mars the complexion, described here by what it does.

clue.text: Ride a bit carelessly and get a mouthful

indicators.note: carelessly means the letters are put down in a disorderly fashion

explanation.surface: A careless rider gets an earful.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter tirade, and to get a mouthful is to receive an angry rebuke.

clue.text: Overstressed by multiple courses

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the next word is read backwards

parts.note: the printed word Overstressed splits in two: its tail is taken as written and turned round; that the whole run sits inside one printed word is a coincidence of the split, not a hiding device

explanation.surface: Someone is overwhelmed by a meal of many courses.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'Overstressed' splits into an indicator 'Over' and the word STRESSED, which reversed gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Desserts are sweet courses, so several of them are multiple courses.

clue.text: In Lent, English celebrate

indicators.note: In puts the English letter inside the word for Lent

parts.note: Lent is a time of fasting, a fast

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether English people celebrate during Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: To feast is to celebrate with lavish eating, a synonym in the festive sense.

clue.text: Drunkards are about, even in Kent

indicators.note: drunkards being about something means they wrap round it

parts.note: soaks is slang for heavy drinkers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drunks are around, even down in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVENOAKS is a commuter town in the English county of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition points to a place located in the county of Kent, which this town is.

clue.text: Ragtimer's weed?

definitions.meaning: Irving Berlin's song ... Ragtime Band names a ragtime bandleader, so the ragtimer's is ...
a tall umbelliferous plant that grows wild as a weed

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe hides in the answer: read one way it is the bandleader's possessive, the other a plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant Smyrnium olusatrum is commonly called alexanders and spreads as a wayside weed.

clue.text: Actor branched out

definitions.meaning: Sir Herbert Beerbohm ... was a famous Victorian actor-manager
a plant that has branched out has grown into a woody trunk with limbs

explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was the actor's surname; a branched woody plant is the second sense.

clue.text: Irish prison officers have taken to the bottle

parts.note: Cork is an Irish city and county
screws is British slang for prison warders

explanation.surface: Irish jailers have turned to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken to the bottle' sounds like drinking, but means implements applied to a bottle to open it.
explanation.definitionFit: Corkscrews are tools applied to wine bottles to draw corks, so they are taken to the bottle.

clue.text: Doctor in dream coatgoing off to war

indicators.note: in puts the doctor's letters inside the rearranged words
going off suggests something exploding, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor in Joseph's coat of many colours heads off to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' rearranges DREAM COAT to ARMED COAT, and MB goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed combat is fighting with weapons, which is what war consists of.

clue.text: Grit Naomi displayed in returning with Ruth

indicators.note: the letters are displayed in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: In the Bible, Naomi shows grit as she goes home with her daughter-in-law Ruth.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Ruth, Naomi returns to Bethlehem from Moab with Ruth.
explanation.definitionFit: Migration is moving from one land to another, as Naomi and Ruth did on returning to Judah.

clue.text: Final performance of an actress?

parts.note: a farewell performance, playfully read as a ditty sung by the film star Gloria Swanson

explanation.definitionFit: A swansong is a final performance, and Gloria Swanson was a film actress.

clue.text: In confusion one girl takes a pill

indicators.note: In puts the single letter inside the confusion word

parts.note: a daze is a state of confusion
I is the Roman numeral one
Pam is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Bewildered, a young woman swallows a tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: Diazepam, sold as Valium, is a sedative usually taken as a pill.

clue.text: It may bear correspondence — with a raven?

definitions.text: It may bear correspondence — with a raven?

parts.words: It may bear correspondence — with a raven?
parts.note: a piece of furniture letters are written on, recalling the Mad Hatter's riddle in Alice in Wonderland about what a raven has in common with it

explanation.walkthrough: The Mad Hatter asks 'Why is a raven like a writing desk?'; 'correspondence' means both letters and a likeness.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk for writing letters bears correspondence, and Lewis Carroll's riddle likens it to a raven.

clue.text: Fellow takes a nap — almost, but not just yet

parts.note: man means fellow

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man has a quick doze, putting things off.
explanation.walkthrough: MANANA is Spanish for tomorrow, used to mean some later time.
explanation.definitionFit: Mañana, Spanish for tomorrow, is used in English to mean at some indefinite later time.

clue.text: One bombardier gets in before another

indicators.note: gets in means the soldier goes inside the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a bombardier is a non-commissioned officer, an NCO

explanation.surface: One artillery soldier gets in ahead of the next.
explanation.walkthrough: A bombardier is a junior NCO rank in the British artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience shouting encore is calling for another song, so it means another.

clue.text: Samson, say, gave up religious observance to become a fascist

indicators.note: giving something up means it is taken away from the word

parts.note: Samson in the Bible was a Nazirite, one under a vow never to cut his hair
a rite is a religious ceremony or observance

explanation.surface: The strongman Samson abandoned his faith and turned to fascism.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nazirite is an Israelite bound by a vow; Samson is the best-known one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nazi is a term for a member of Hitler's fascist party, and loosely any fascist.

clue.text: Timekeeper?

parts.note: read literally, something that keeps hold of a timepiece rather than a person who records time

explanation.definitionFit: A chain fastened to a pocket watch keeps the timepiece secure, so it is a keeper of the watch.

clue.text: Speak of your fault to the church — it's easy

indicators.note: speak of means the word is said rather than spelt

parts.note: a sin is a moral fault

explanation.surface: Confessing your failings to the church is simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinch is something very easy, as in 'it's a cinch'.

clue.text: Little sheep rejecting a doctor for a false god

indicators.note: rejecting means these letters are thrown out of the word

parts.note: baa-lamb is a nursery word for a lamb
A plus MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: A lamb turns away the vet and follows an idol.
explanation.walkthrough: Baal was a Canaanite deity condemned as a false god in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Baal was a Canaanite deity whom the Old Testament condemns as an idol.

clue.text: Instrument made by hunter out of broken harp

indicators.note: the hunter is the outside of the word, made out of with the broken harp inside

parts.note: Orion is the great hunter of Greek myth and the constellation

indicators.note: broken tells us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: A hunter fashions a musical instrument from the pieces of a smashed harp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' reads as 'made from', but here it means the hunter's name forms the outside, with the shuffled instrument letters set within it.
explanation.definitionFit: An orpharion is a Renaissance plucked string instrument related to the lute.

clue.text: Books are rejected but could be an inspiration

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the whole run is read in reverse

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books
taken as written

explanation.surface: Turned-down manuscripts can still spark an idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns OT + ARE into ERATO, the Muse of lyric poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses, figures who inspire poets.

clue.text: It makes music from a mangle

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is made out of these letters once reorganised

explanation.surface: A clothes wringer turns out a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The mangle, an old laundry wringer, suggests squeezing the letters of A MANGLE into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamelan is an Indonesian percussion orchestra, so it is something that makes music.

clue.text: Reluctant guest hogs tea when it's free

indicators.note: letters set free are released to fall in a new order

explanation.surface: A guest eats all the tea whenever it comes at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is held against their will, a guest who would rather not stay.
